items.title: ci: migrate cosign to v3 and dual-publish image signatures
items.body:
<!--
Copilot: Fill all sections. Prefer short, concrete answers.
If a checkbox is selected, add a brief explanation.
-->

## Summary
<!-- In 1–2 sentences: what does this PR do? -->
Upgrade cosign from v2.6.5 to v3.1.3 and publish **both legacy signatures and native Sigstore bundles for the identical immutable image digest**. Unmodified verification commands work with the tested v2/v3 clients; the user-facing verification documentation initially added by this PR has been removed as requested.

## Why
<!-- Why is this change needed? Link issues or discussions. -->
Follow-up to [#3370](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/pull/3370), which deferred v3 because its bundle defaults could break consumers. No issue is automatically closed.

Both v2.6.5 and v3.1.3 fix GHSA-fx35-mq7g-6g98. v3.1.3 was the latest stable checked on 2026-10-02. The original implementation retained only legacy signatures; this revision implements the user's explicit request for dual publication without a consumer command migration or extra repository docs.

## What changed
<!-- Bullet list of concrete changes. -->
- Keep the existing SHA-pinned installer and select **cosign v3.1.3**.
- Sign once per repository/index digest in two sequential, required steps: legacy `cosign sign --yes --new-bundle-format=false --use-signing-config=false --registry-referrers-mode=legacy`, then native **`cosign sign --yes`**, with v3's default bundle format and TUF-provided signing-service configuration.
- Both steps use exactly `"${REGISTRY}/${IMAGE_NAME}@${DIGEST}"`, with `DIGEST` from the same build output. Tags are aliases to that image, not separate subjects; signing once avoids accumulating identical bundles for every alias.
- Preserve GitHub OIDC/Fulcio, transparency logging, existing permissions, digest signing, and PR publication/signing exclusions. Either signing step failing fails the job; native signing is skipped if legacy signing fails.
- Correct the pre-existing misleading private-image comment: `--yes` also consents to public transparency-log disclosure.
- Remove `docs/verify-artifacts.md` and all README/SECURITY additions introduced by this PR. Pre-existing docs are unchanged. **The aggregate PR diff is now only `.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml`.**

Only the Docker workflow uses cosign. The release workflow and `.goreleaser.yaml` use GitHub build-provenance attestations for archives/checksums, not cosign blob signatures; those remain unchanged.

## Consumer impact and supported limits

**Tested unchanged command behavior, not universal client compatibility:** cosign **v2.5.3**, **v2.6.5**, and **v3.1.3** all verify the same dual-signed digest without any format/discovery flag. This was proved both locally and against the real user-authorized GHCR test image with GitHub OIDC/Fulcio/Rekor checks enabled. v2.5.3 is an older compatibility-test client, not a recommendation to use an unpatched release.

| Client/path | Observed behavior on the dual-signed digest |
| --- | --- |
| v2.5.3, default `cosign verify` | Verifies the legacy `.sig` signature. |
| v2.6.5, default `cosign verify` | Auto-discovers and verifies the native bundle. |
| v3.1.3, default `cosign verify` | Auto-discovers and verifies the native bundle. |
| v3.1.3, `--new-bundle-format=false` | Explicitly verifies the legacy `.sig` signature. |

**Important evidence:** v2.6.5 auto-discovery overrides even `--new-bundle-format=false` when native bundles exist. We did not mislabel that result as legacy verification. Its default image command verified legacy before the native pass; its `verify-blob` also cryptographically verified the exact retained legacy payload/signature downloaded from `.sig` storage after dual publication. The older v2.5.3 default image command and v3's explicit legacy path verified `.sig` directly while native bundles coexisted.

Native verification output is not byte-for-byte the legacy JSON: the native `critical.type` is `https://sigstore.dev/cosign/sign/v1`, and `critical.identity.docker-reference` includes the digest. Consumers parsing those values or supplying custom legacy certificate/root flags need separate compatibility review. Retaining `.sig` does not force v2.6.5 to choose it. Unsupported/untested versions, offline/custom trust setups, policy engines, and registries other than tested GHCR/local `registry:3` are **not** claimed universally compatible.

The legacy pass retains the legacy image payload, `.sig` storage and Rekor v1 defaults. `--use-signing-config=false` is necessary as well as the format opt-out: v3 rejects legacy image signing with its default signing config unless a local bundle is supplied. Native signing uses protobuf-defined Sigstore bundles serialized as JSON, an OCI referring artifact, and default TUF signing-service discovery. On both tested registries discovery used the **OCI referrers fallback tag**, distinct from `.sig`. This does not assume the registry serves the native referrers HTTP API.

The real native bundle's media type was `application/vnd.dev.sigstore.bundle.v0.3+json`; its transparency entry was `dsse` v0.0.1, with inclusion promise/proof and a `rekor.sigstore.dev` checkpoint. The legacy entry was `hashedrekord`. Native defaults **must not be described as necessarily selecting Rekor v2**: current TUF configuration selected the observed service. `--new-bundle-format` remains supported but deprecated in v3.1.3. `cosign verify` does not accept the signing-only `--registry-referrers-mode` flag.

Research: [v3 announcement](https://blog.sigstore.dev/cosign-3-0-available/), [v3.1.3 release](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/releases/tag/v3.1.3), [signing-config validation](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/blob/v3.1.3/cmd/cosign/cli/signcommon/common.go), [v3 discovery](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/blob/v3.1.3/cmd/cosign/cli/verify/verify.go), [v2.6.5 discovery](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/blob/v2.6.5/cmd/cosign/cli/verify/verify.go), and [OCI publication](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/blob/v3.1.3/pkg/oci/remote/write.go).

## Real GHCR / GitHub OIDC / Rekor test

**Passed on the reviewed commit `813e3fa03465d1aee39f70771349c15ae68bb839`:** [authorized isolated branch dispatch](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/actions/runs/36997176977), both signing steps successful.

The user explicitly authorized isolated branch/test publication. Before dispatch, the pinned metadata action and ref rules were inspected: branch dispatch cannot generate semver/tag aliases; `edge` requires default branch `main`; schedule is inactive; explicit `latest` is disabled for a branch; automatic `latest` is not emitted for branch/sha tags. Actual run metadata confirmed **only**:

```text
ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server:sammorrowdrums-cosign-v3-signing-migration
ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server:sha-813e3fa
```

Both resolve to the same multi-platform index digest:

```text
sha256:4a5a05533a67518a32fed05da34f1b64bf8d3bcc8148053eced9725a85aba77d
```

Read-only registry inspection confirmed a retained legacy `.sig` manifest with certificate/Rekor material and a separate OCI referrers fallback index containing the native bundle. Both signatures' subjects match the digest above. No `latest`, `edge`, main/nightly, or release/version aliases were published by this dispatch. No Git tags were pushed; the GoReleaser/release workflows were not triggered; nothing was merged.

**Exact verification command, unchanged for all three tested client versions — passed with no insecure bypass flags:**

```sh
IMAGE='ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server@sha256:4a5a05533a67518a32fed05da34f1b64bf8d3bcc8148053eced9725a85aba77d'
IDENTITY='https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml@refs/heads/sammorrowdrums-cosign-v3-signing-migration'
ISSUER='https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com'
cosign verify --certificate-identity "$IDENTITY" --certificate-oidc-issuer "$ISSUER" "$IMAGE"
```

v3.1.3 also passed that command with `--new-bundle-format=false`, proving the real legacy certificate/log path remains valid. Default v2.6.5/v3.1.3 rejected the wrong `refs/heads/main` certificate identity and an incorrect OIDC issuer. Verification checked the exact digest, workflow/ref identity, issuer, certificate trust, and transparency material. An empty, isolated `DOCKER_CONFIG` was used for anonymous reads; user registry credentials/configuration were not modified.

The branch test now covers **real GHCR publication, v3 keyless issuance, and public Rekor material**, not just a generated-key proxy. Remaining release gate: confirm any additional supported consumers/policies and the actual release/prerelease ref identity through the normal maintainer-controlled release process. A prerelease tag/ref was not authorized or exercised by this branch test; native HTTP referrers API mode, key/log rotation, parallel same-digest writers, and injected public-service outages were not tested.

## Partial publication and retry semantics

Publication is **not atomic**. Image aliases are pushed before signatures. If legacy signing fails, CI fails and the native pass is skipped; an unsigned image or partial legacy upload may already exist. If native signing fails, CI fails, but a valid legacy signature and possibly partial native upload/log entries may remain. No failure is masked with `continue-on-error`, `always()`, or success-shaped fallback.

Retry the signing commands for the **recorded immutable digest**, then verify both formats and the expected identity. Local tests injected native failure after the legacy pass and proved retry completes dual publication without changing the existing `.sig` manifest. Two full same-digest reruns and a second signing key preserved all previous signatures. Native bundles can accumulate on rerun; this is safe append/retention behavior, **not exactly-once/idempotent artifact counts**. A full workflow rerun may rebuild a different digest because metadata changes, so it is not guaranteed to repair the old partially signed digest. Do not delete prior `.sig`/referrer artifacts as an automatic cleanup or silently accept a partial publication.

## MCP impact
<!-- Select one or more. If selected, add 1–2 sentences. -->
- [x] No tool or API changes — publisher workflow only; toolsnaps unchanged and passing.
- [ ] Tool schema or behavior changed
- [ ] New tool added

## Prompts tested (tool changes only)
<!-- If you changed or added tools, list example prompts you tested. -->
<!-- Include prompts that trigger the tool and describe the use case. -->
<!-- Example: "List all open issues in the repo assigned to me" -->
- N/A: no MCP tool changes.

## Security / limits
<!-- Select if relevant. Add a short note if checked. -->
- [ ] No security or limits impact
- [x] Auth / permissions considered — same workflow OIDC and packages permissions; both passes issue ephemeral Fulcio certificates; real exact identity/issuer verification passed.
- [x] Data exposure, filtering, or token/size limits considered — two public signing/log entries per digest may be generated; public-log disclosure is unchanged. Only local disposable-key tests disabled tlog upload/verification, never production or real consumer verification.

## Tool renaming
- [ ] I am renaming tools as part of this PR (e.g. a part of a consolidation effort)
   - [ ] I have added the new tool aliases in `deprecated_tool_aliases.go` 
- [x] I am not renaming tools as part of this PR — names/schemas unchanged.

Note: if you're renaming tools, you *must* add the tool aliases. For more information on how to do so, please refer to the [official docs](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/blob/main/docs/tool-renaming.md).

## Lint & tests
<!-- Check what you ran. If not run, explain briefly. -->
- [x] Linted locally with `./script/lint` — `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.8 TMPDIR="$PWD/bin/lint-tmp" sh script/lint`: **passed, 0 issues**, using the branch's pinned toolchain/linter.
- [x] Tested locally with `./script/test` — `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.8 sh script/test`: **passed full race suite/toolsnaps**, after lint.

| Exact command/check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `actionlint -oneline -ignore 'label "ubuntu-latest-xl" is unknown' .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml` | Passed; only the pre-existing custom runner diagnostic excluded. |
| `cosign sign --yes --help` and legacy command with all three compatibility flags plus `--help` on v3.1.3 | Passed flag parsing; both actual formats also signed locally and in the real dispatch. |
| `python3 test_dual.py` (session-only harness; checksum-verified upstream v2.5.3/v2.6.5/v3.1.3 binaries, generated keys, disposable loopback `registry:3`) | Passed coexistence, exact signature subjects/storage, default discovery and verification, retained signatures across two reruns/second signer, native failure/retry, wrong-key rejection, and tampering with **each** format. |
| `python3 test_workflow.py` (session-only harness reading the actual YAML and executing its commands with a failing cosign stub under `bash -eo pipefail`) | Passed: successful flow invokes both commands on identical digest; legacy failure exits 42 with native skipped; native failure exits 43; both steps exclude PRs and cannot continue on error. |
| `python3 verify_public.py sha256:4a5a05533a67518a32fed05da34f1b64bf8d3bcc8148053eced9725a85aba77d` (read-only session harness) | Passed actual test-tag/digest equality, both stored formats, unmodified real v2/v3 verification, v3 legacy verification, and wrong identity/issuer negatives. |
| `git diff cd502333 -- README.md SECURITY.md` and file absence check | Passed: original docs unchanged; new verification file removed. |
| `git diff --check` | Passed. |

Local signing commands used generated keys and **only locally** added `--key test.key --tlog-upload=false`; the native test also used `--use-signing-config=false` to avoid public service use. Local verification used `--key test.pub --insecure-ignore-tlog`. These tests did not pretend to cover production service discovery; the subsequent authorized real dispatch used the exact unmodified publisher commands with GitHub OIDC/Rekor and covered that gap.

The local tamper test replaced every legacy signature's bytes, then every native DSSE signature's bytes under its own discovery index, asserting cryptographic failure rather than merely missing signatures. Valid native signatures still verified when legacy was corrupted; corrupt native bundles were rejected by default v2.6.5/v3.1.3 **without silently falling back** to a valid legacy signature. Generated-key wrong-key checks failed in both formats. Local registries were stopped; fixtures are outside the repository. No tests require consumers to change their commands.

**Fresh hosted CI for `813e3fa0`: 17 passing checks, 1 failing lint check.** Docker PR build, all Go platform builds, CodeQL, docs-check and MCP diffs passed; both PR signing steps were correctly skipped. The real isolated dispatch additionally passed both signing steps.

The failing [PR lint run](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/actions/runs/36996702609) uses newer linter/go-github changes now on `main` and reports pre-existing `govet` inline/type-parameter-inference errors in `pkg/github/discussions.go:102–104`. Current [main lint](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/actions/runs/36994963058) also fails with that same class of errors in untouched code; main's [go-github v92 merge lint](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/actions/runs/36994860918) failed too. The aggregate PR modifies none of those code/linter surfaces. That independent base regression was reported to the dependency coordinator and **must be resolved before merge**; this PR does not suppress it or mix in unrelated Go changes.

`script/generate-docs` is not applicable: no MCP tools/toolsets changed. Live PAT-based e2e and a release-tag build were not run.

## Docs

- [x] Not needed — user explicitly requested removing this PR's extra signing/verification docs. Engineering evidence, version limits, and rollout/rollback are preserved here instead; existing unrelated docs are untouched.
- [ ] Updated (README / docs / examples)

## Rollout plan

1. Review the successful isolated branch dispatch and real consumer verification above. Confirm supported older clients/policy consumers and accept v2.6.5's native auto-discovery/output differences; do not claim universal command/output compatibility.
2. Resolve the independent current-main lint regression and require applicable checks to pass before merge. Release maintainers should verify actual prerelease/release identity and any policy-specific tooling through the normal authorized release process; no additional tag/publication is automatically triggered by this PR work.
3. Merge only after approval. Main pushes and scheduled Docker runs publish too, so merge itself starts rollout; monitor both required signing steps and verify both artifacts at the first main/nightly and next stable release digests.
4. Assign an owner/exit criteria for removing legacy publication. Deprecated v3 compatibility flags, Rekor v1 availability, native bundles/referrer discovery, and any future v4 migration require an explicit follow-up decision. Keep both formats until that decision is made.

## Rollback plan

For a native-publication regression, remove/disable the native step and keep legacy signing with the tested flags; if necessary restore the installer to security-fixed **v2.6.5** as well (its CLI accepts those flags). Do not claim that removing the step removes already-published native bundles: v2.6.5 can still discover those and cannot be forced to legacy with the false flag. Preserve existing signature/referrer artifacts; do not delete production `.sig`/referrer tags automatically.

For an unsigned/partial publication, have an authorized maintainer restore the known-good publisher and re-sign the **recorded affected immutable digest** in the required format(s), then verify both subjects and identities. A full rebuild may produce a new digest and is not guaranteed to repair the old one. Do not repoint production aliases or push/modify Git release tags as automated rollback. No merge has been performed.

**Maintainer decisions:** supported consumer/policy matrix and native output compatibility, release-ref gate, independent lint fix, signature-retention/duplicate-bundle policy, and owner/deadline for eventually retiring legacy publication.

## Summary
<!-- In 1–2 sentences: what does this PR do? -->
Upgrade `github.com/google/go-github` from `v89.0.1-0.20260728185857-34349a88bac3` to stable `v92.0.0`, migrating imports and affected requests without changing MCP tool names, schemas, or output contracts.

## Why
<!-- Why is this change needed? Link issues or discussions. -->
Follow-up to #3370, which deferred this major-version migration. The branch starts from the latest fetched `main`, `cd502333` (#3370).

## What changed
<!-- Bullet list of concrete changes. -->
- Update all production, unit-test, and e2e imports to `/v92`; tidy without changing other dependency versions or the Go 1.26.8 directive.
- Use value-based `IssueCommentRequest{Body: body}` for comment creation/updating; replace `Issues.EditComment` with `Issues.UpdateComment`. Preserve POST/PATCH bodies, validation, error handling, and minimal ID/URL outputs. Add a creation request-body assertion; updating already asserts its payload.
- Pass the raw branch to `ListRulesForBranch`: v92 escapes it internally. Existing slash/hash/percent regression tests caught double escaping and now pass unchanged.
- Regenerate platform license reports and move the unchanged BSD license from the v89 path to v92.
- Retain supported `github.Ptr` with a narrow deprecation-warning exclusion. Pinned golangci-lint v2.9.0 misreports SA4006 for Go 1.26 `new(expression)`; trial upgrades introduce unrelated baseline findings. No checks are disabled globally; linter/CI versions remain unchanged. Remove this compatibility exclusion in a separate linter upgrade.

Reviewed published release notes/changelogs for [v90](https://github.com/google/go-github/releases/tag/v90.0.0), [v91](https://github.com/google/go-github/releases/tag/v91.0.0), and [v92](https://github.com/google/go-github/releases/tag/v92.0.0), plus tagged commit comparisons. Complete breaking-change disposition:

| Release | Breaking change | Repository handling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All | Major module import path | Migrate every Go import and exported library surface to `/v92`, including e2e. |
| v90 | Dependabot secrets request/response refactor | No secret-management calls; alert APIs unchanged. |
| v90 | Repository merge/upstream merge value requests and required value fields | No affected calls; PR merging uses a different API. |
| v90 | Template repo value request and string `Name` | No template-creation calls. |

items.title: fix(pull_request_reviews): Update pending pull request review lookup to work when the authenticated actor is a Copilot bot
items.body:
## Summary

Pull request review tools which pull the current pending review for the user don't work when authenticated with a Copilot installation (server-to-server/S2S) token.

This fixes it by changing how we pull the current pending review to to be more resilient to the specific implementation of Copilot bots.

## Why

Many of our pull request review tools rely on using the GitHub GraphQL API to look up the current pending review:

* add_comment_to_pending_review / add_pull_request_review_comment
* submit_pending / submit_pending_pull_request_review
* delete_pending / delete_pending_pull_request_review

Under the hood, we do this by fetching the current `viewer.login` and then fetching reviewers where the `author` matches that login.

This is currently broken for Copilot bots. When authenticated as Copilot cloud agent, the GraphQL API reports `Copilot` for `viewer.login`, but this isn't the bot's _real_ login.

The real login is `copilot-swe-agent` (the bot identity represented as `copilot-swe-agent[bot]` elsewhere). 

Filtering the reviews connection with the reported viewer login therefore returns no pending review, so adding comments, submitting, and deleting pending reviews fail.

GraphQL node IDs are stable across those representations, so they are a more reliable identity key.

No linked issue.

## What changed

- Query `viewer.id` instead of `viewer.login`.
- Load `PENDING` reviews without an author-login filter, paginate them, and select the first review whose author node ID matches the viewer node ID.
- Select IDs through concrete `Actor` fragments because the interface does not expose `id`; compare only globally unique node IDs because this token presents the viewer as `User` and the review author as `Bot`.
- Share the lookup across comment, submit, and delete operations, with coverage that skips another user's pending review before selecting the viewer's review.

## MCP impact

- [ ] No tool or API changes
- [x] Tool schema or behavior changed
- [ ] New tool added

The schemas are unchanged. The existing pending-review operations now work when the authenticated viewer's reported login does not match the review author's real login.

## Prompts tested (tool changes only)

- "Add this comment to my pending review."
- "Submit my pending review as a comment."
- "Delete my pending review."

Live validation on this draft used the built MCP server over stdio to create a pending review, add a line comment, and submit it. The old `author: "Copilot"` query returned no review, while the new query matched viewer and author node ID `BOT_kgDOC9w8XQ`.

## Security / limits

- [ ] No security or limits impact
- [x] Auth / permissions considered
- [x] Data exposure, filtering, or token/size limits considered

The API currently returns only the viewer's own pending reviews, but the client still matches author ID defensively in case that behavior changes. Results are fetched in pages of 100 and stop as soon as the viewer's review is found.

## Tool renaming

- [ ] I am renaming tools as part of this PR (e.g. a part of a consolidation effort)
   - [ ] I have added the new tool aliases in `deprecated_tool_aliases.go`
- [x] I am not renaming tools as part of this PR

## Lint & tests

- [ ] Linted locally with `./script/lint`
- [x] Tested locally with `./script/test`

`gofmt -s`, `go vet ./...`, focused tests, the full race-enabled test suite, and the live MCP create/comment/submit flow pass. `./script/lint` could not install `golangci-lint` because its installer host is blocked in this environment; running the pinned linter through Go modules reached a Go export-data compatibility error.

## Docs

- [ ] Updated (README / docs / examples)

items.title: Add granular tools to hide and unhide issue comments, PR review comments and PR reviews
items.body:
## Summary
Adds granular tools to hide (minimize) and unhide (unminimize) comments on issues and pull requests, using the GraphQL `minimizeComment` / `unminimizeComment` mutations. There is one pair per object type, behind the `issues_granular` and `pull_requests_granular` feature flags.

## Why
The server has no way to hide spam, off-topic, outdated or resolved comments. Hiding is only available through GraphQL; REST has no equivalent. Related: #3321 / #3329, which surface `minimized_reason` when reading comments.

## What changed
| Tools | Toolset / flag | Hides | Arguments (all required) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hide_issue_comment` / `unhide_issue_comment` | `issues` / `issues_granular` | Issue comments and PR conversation comments (both are issue comments in the API) | `owner`, `repo`, `comment_id` |
| `hide_pull_request_review_comment` / `unhide_pull_request_review_comment` | `pull_requests` / `pull_requests_granular` | Inline PR diff comments | `owner`, `repo`, `comment_id` |
| `hide_pull_request_review` / `unhide_pull_request_review` | `pull_requests` / `pull_requests_granular` | PR review bodies | `owner`, `repo`, `pullNumber`, `review_id` |

- The `hide_*` tools also require `classifier` (`SPAM`, `ABUSE`, `OFF_TOPIC`, `OUTDATED`, `DUPLICATE`, `RESOLVED`, `LOW_QUALITY`).
- There are no conditional arguments: every property in every schema is required.
- Callers pass the numeric REST IDs returned by the existing read tools. Each tool fetches the matching REST resource to get its GraphQL `node_id`, then runs the mutation. It returns `{node_id, is_minimized, minimized_reason}`.
- All six tools are built by one helper in `pkg/github/comment_minimize.go`, parameterised by a `commentVisibilityTarget` for each object type. The exported constructors (`GranularHideIssueComment`, etc.) are one-liners in `issues_granular.go` and `pullrequests_granular.go`.
- Argument names follow the neighbouring granular tools: `comment_id` as in the reaction tools, and `pullNumber` as in the other PR tools.
- Toolsnaps, the granular toolset tests and `docs/feature-flags.md` are updated.

## MCP impact
- [ ] No tool or API changes
- [ ] Tool schema or behavior changed
- [x] New tool added

Six new write tools, each visible only when its feature flag is enabled.

## Prompts tested (tool changes only)
- "Hide the last comment on issue #42 as spam"
- "Hide the review comments on PR #7 that have been addressed as resolved"
- "Hide the outdated review summary on PR #7"
- "Unhide the comment I accidentally hid on issue #42"

**End-to-end test against the live API:** I built the server and ran it over stdio with `--toolsets issues,pull_requests --features issues_granular,pull_requests_granular`, driven by a small MCP client. It created real content on #3351 (a temporary test issue) and on this PR. It called each hide tool and then the matching unhide tool, and checked `isMinimized` / `minimizedReason` with an independent GraphQL query after each call:

| Object | Tools | Classifier | Hide | Unhide |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Issue comment | `hide_issue_comment` / `unhide_issue_comment` | `SPAM` | ✅ | ✅ |
| PR conversation comment | `hide_issue_comment` / `unhide_issue_comment` | `OFF_TOPIC` | ✅ | ✅ |
| PR review (inline) comment | `hide_pull_request_review_comment` / `unhide_…` | `OUTDATED` | ✅ | ✅ |
| PR review body | `hide_pull_request_review` / `unhide_…` | `RESOLVED` | ✅ | ✅ |

Error cases also behaved correctly against the live API, with no side effects:
- An issue comment ID passed to the review comment tool, and the reverse, both return a clear 404 error.
- A review ID with the wrong `pullNumber` returns 404.
- A missing `pullNumber` is rejected before any API call.
- An invalid classifier is rejected by GraphQL, and the comment is left unchanged.

Each flag was also checked to expose exactly its own tools: no flags gives none, `issues_granular` gives the issue pair, and `pull_requests_granular` gives the four PR tools.

The test comments have been deleted and #3351 is closed. One test review stays on this PR with its body edited, because GitHub doesn't allow deleting submitted reviews.

## Security / limits
- [ ] No security or limits impact
- [x] Auth / permissions considered
- [ ] Data exposure, filtering, or token/size limits considered

Requires the `repo` scope, like the other granular write tools. GitHub itself enforces that the caller has triage/write access or is the author; permission errors from the mutation are returned as tool errors.

## Tool renaming
- [ ] I am renaming tools as part of this PR (e.g. a part of a consolidation effort)
   - [ ] I have added the new tool aliases in `deprecated_tool_aliases.go` 
- [x] I am not renaming tools as part of this PR

## Lint & tests
- [x] Linted locally with `./script/lint`
- [x] Tested locally with `./script/test`

Lint was run with Go 1.25 and golangci-lint v2.9.0 to match CI. The table-driven unit tests cover the following, and the new code has 90–100% statement coverage:
- hide and unhide for all three object types
- not-found for each object type
- a response with no node ID
- mutation failures
- each missing required argument

items.title: Always enable MCP Apps UI; remove remote_mcp_ui_apps flag gate
items.body:
## Why

The `remote_mcp_ui_apps` feature flag is at 100% rollout on the hosted (remote) server, so MCP Apps is always on in production. In this repo it was still off by default unless enabled through `--features`/`X-MCP-Features` or insiders mode. This PR removes that difference so the OSS server matches the shipped remote behavior.

## What changed

- **Inventory:** `_meta.ui` is now always emitted. It's stripped only when the client explicitly doesn't advertise the `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` capability, which is the spec-conformant check. The flag branch is gone from `ToolsForRegistration`, `shouldStripMCPAppsMetadata` and `RequiredFeatures`, and `mcpAppsFeatureFlag` is deleted.
- **`ui_get`:** no longer feature-gated. It is app-only (`_meta.ui.visibility: ["app"]`), so for clients without the UI capability, app-only tools are now left out entirely. Previously, stripping `_meta.ui` would have exposed it as an ordinary model-visible tool.
- **Form deferral:** `shouldDeferToForm` no longer checks `remote_mcp_ui_apps`. Write tools hand off to their MCP App form by default for UI-capable clients. `mcp_apps_disable_form_deferral` is unchanged and remains the long-lived opt-out.
- **Feature flags:** removed `MCPAppsFeatureFlag` and its entries in `AllowedFeatureFlags` and `InsidersFeatureFlags`. `featureEnabledRule`/`featureDisabledRule` stay because other flags use them.
- **Tests:** updated for the new defaults, plus new tests showing app-only tools (including the real `ui_get`) are left out for clients without UI support and kept when support is present or unknown.
- **Docs:** regenerated with `script/generate-docs`, so the README now lists the MCP App UI URIs and `ui_get`, and the `remote_mcp_ui_apps` sections are gone from `feature-flags.md`/`insiders-features.md`. The MCP Apps section in `server-configuration.md` now says MCP Apps is always on.

## Follow-up for github/github-mcp-server-remote

After this merges, github/github-mcp-server-remote should:
- bump its `github-mcp-server` dependency to pick this up;
- update the tests that reference the now-deleted `githubMcp.MCPAppsFeatureFlag` (`internal/featureflags/flags_test.go`, `pkg/mcp/inventory/inventory_test.go`);
- drop the stale `remote_mcp_ui_apps` comment in `internal/featureflags/flags.go`.

* Add hide_comment and unhide_comment granular issue tools

Add two tools behind the issues_granular feature flag that hide
(minimize) and unhide (unminimize) comments via the GraphQL
minimizeComment/unminimizeComment mutations.

They support issue and pull request conversation comments, pull
request review comments, and pull request review bodies. Callers
pass the numeric REST ID plus a comment_type; the tool resolves the
GraphQL node ID via the matching REST endpoint before mutating.

* Use realistic minimizedReason values in hide_comment test mocks

GitHub returns minimizedReason in lowercase, hyphenated form (e.g.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Split hide/unhide comment tools per object type

Replace hide_comment/unhide_comment, which took a comment_type
argument, with a granular pair per object type:

- hide_issue_comment / unhide_issue_comment (issues_granular):
  issue comments and pull request conversation comments
- hide_pull_request_review_comment / unhide_pull_request_review_comment
  (pull_requests_granular): inline pull request review comments
- hide_pull_request_review / unhide_pull_request_review
  (pull_requests_granular): pull request review bodies

Every argument is now unconditionally required, so the schemas no
longer need prose explaining which arguments apply to which type. The
six tools are built from one shared helper, parameterised by a
commentVisibilityTarget that describes each object type and how to
resolve its GraphQL node ID.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Validate classifier and IDs before calling the GitHub API

JSON schema constraints (enum, minimum) aren't enforced when tool
arguments are unmarshalled, so an invalid classifier or a negative ID
previously reached GitHub and surfaced as a confusing 404 or GraphQL
error. Reject them up front with a clear argument error instead.
